description: Key facts for this chapter, written by hand from the chapter text. Every entry links to the section that explains it.

people.name: Marcus Furius Camillus
people.text: Dictator who took Veii through a tunnel; in Livy’s story he also drove the Gauls out of Rome.

people.name: Brennus
people.text: The Gallic chief who won at the Allia and said “Woe to the vanquished!”

people.name: Marcus Manlius
people.text: Former consul woken by the sacred geese, who threw the first Gaul off the Capitoline.

people.name: Lucius Albinus
people.text: Citizen who carried the Vestal Virgins and the sacred objects to Caere on his wagon.

people.name: Marcus Papirius
people.text: Old former magistrate who struck a Gaul with his ivory staff, starting the massacre.

people.name: Aruns
people.text: The man who, Livy says, brought the Gauls to Clusium to take revenge.

people.name: Gaius Licinius Stolo
people.text: Tribune of the plebs who led the ten-year campaign for the new laws; later fined for breaking his own land limit.

people.name: Lucius Sextius Lateranus
people.text: Licinius’s fellow tribune, Rome’s first plebeian consul in 366 BC.

people.name: Lucius Genucius
people.text: Tribune whose law of 342 BC made sharing the consulship regular.

dates.text: Consular tribunes begin to replace the consuls in many years.
The Gauls win at the Allia and sack Rome (traditional date; historians prefer c. 387 BC).
Licinius and Sextius begin their campaign.
The Senate accepts the laws of Licinius and Sextius.
Lucius Sextius becomes the first plebeian consul.
The law of Genucius: one consul is regularly a plebeian.
